links.outcome: Flesch-Kincaid grade level of original ChatGPT responses versus sixth-grade recommendation
links.effect: Original responses averaged FK grade 11.09 ± 1.47 and reading ease 39.12 ± 8.25; 28 of 30 (93.3%) required at least college-level education.
links.quote: Similar to other studies [ 15 , 32 , 40 ], the original responses generated by ChatGPT in our research were written at much higher educational levels than the sixth grade reading level recommended by the National Institutes of Health and the American Medical Association [ 13 , 29 ].

links.outcome: Readability and accuracy of AI patient education responses after simplification prompts
links.effect: Simplify prompt lowered FK grade from 11.09 to 8.16; sixth-grade prompt gave 7.09. Accuracy remained high (no unsatisfactory responses) across prompt types.
links.quote: For simplified responses, the average Flesch‐Kincaid Grade Level for all responses was 8.16 ± 1.46 which correlates approximately to the reading level of an eighth grader.

links.outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT 4.0 answers to PAO questions graded by surgeons against literature
links.effect: 98.3% of responses rated excellent or satisfactory requiring minimal clarification; no responses unsatisfactory; interrater kappa 0.5.
links.quote: ChatGPT was able to give excellent or satisfactory responses to all questions given regarding PAO with most requiring minimal or no clarification (98.3%), including responses that were simplified using specific prompts.

unlisted_practices: Prompting the LLM to simplify or write at a specified reading grade level to improve patient-facing readability

links.effect: 98.3% were graded excellent or satisfactory requiring minimal clarification for accuracy/comprehensiveness.
links.quote: Regarding accuracy and comprehensiveness, 98.3% of responses were graded as "excellent" or "satisfactory, requiring minimal clarification."

links.effect: Grade level improved from 11.09±1.47 original to 8.16±1.46 simplified and 7.09±1.23 sixth-grade, but remained above sixth grade.
links.quote: Readability analysis revealed an average Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level corresponding to an 11th-grade reading level (11.09 ± 1.47) and a mean Reading Ease score requiring college level reading comprehension (39.12 ± 8.25) for original responses, 8th-grade reading level (8.16 ± 1.46) requiring high school to college level reading comprehension (51.53 ± 9.62) for simplified responses, and 7th-grade reading level (7.09 ± 1.23) requiring high school level reading comprehension (62.46 ± 7.48) for 6th grade responses.

links.outcome: reading level of generated patient responses
links.effect: 28 of 30 original responses (93.3%) required at least college-level education to comprehend (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level >= 12.5 or Reading Ease <= 50.0), averaging an 11th-grade reading level (11.09 +/- 1.47).
links.quote: Twenty‐eight responses (93.3%) required at least a college‐level education to comprehend (Flesch‐Kincaid Grade Level ≥ 12.5 or Flesch‐Kincaid Reading Ease ≤ 50.0).
